item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 5, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Jacobs Media founder Fred Jacobs is stepping down as President at the end of the year after 43 years leading the company. His brother, Paul Jacobs, will take over as President, while Fred becomes Chairman. Fred will remain involved in the company's Techsurveys and select consulting projects. The leadership transition will bring a greater focus on digital transformation and revenue growth for broadcasters.
In television news,
TEGNA has expanded Tom Cury’s leadership role, naming him President and General Manager of KVUE in Austin while he continues leading KENS in San Antonio. Cury has headed KENS since 2015, overseeing innovative streaming programming and award-winning community initiatives. He’ll now lead operations at both Texas television stations, strengthening collaboration while maintaining each station’s local focus.
In media business news,
U.S. job openings held steady at 7.5 million in September, while workers quitting their jobs climbed to 3.4 million, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. In the Information sector, which includes media, openings increased to 116,000, with hiring also on the rise. For more details, visit Media Jobs Report dot com.
In podcasting news,
Podscribe's October podcast rankings show Crime Junkie leading audio reach with 16.4 million listeners. Spotify remains the top publisher with more than 304 million monthly plays, while iHeartMedia jumped 63 percent to 177 million. On the advertising side, Quince topped spending at 6.7 million dollars, with SimpliSafe recording one of the month's biggest increases. For the complete story and full podcast, publisher and advertiser rankings, visit Media Jobs Report dot com.
In public media news,
NPR’s popular comedy news quiz “Wait Wait... Don’t Tell Me!” is coming to Rhode Island! Host Peter Sagal brings the Peabody Award-winning show to the Providence Performing Arts Center on December tenth. Presented by Ocean State Media, the live event will feature special guests and plenty of laughs. Tickets are on sale now.
In television news,
WSAW News Channel 7 has promoted Gunnar Tessmer to Director of Sales, overseeing four television properties in north central Wisconsin. Tessmer joined the station in 2017 and most recently served as Multimedia and Digital Sales Manager. A Wisconsin native and University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point graduate, Tessmer says he's excited to continue helping local businesses grow through television and digital advertising.
And finally,
Lady A is bringing the holiday spirit to ABC as hosts of the 17th annual CMA Country Christmas, airing Tuesday, December 1st. The star-studded special features performances by Dan + Shay, Trisha Yearwood, Jordan Davis, Zach Top, Lindsey Stirling and more. Catch it on ABC at 9 Eastern, 8 Central, or stream it the next day on Disney+ and Hulu.
Find more media news, jobs, industry resources and free tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
